name: South Africa
summary: SARS publishes worked examples that pass its own modulus-10 (Luhn) check digit: an income tax reference, a PAYE/SDL/UIF reference and an ID number. ICASA reserves the geographic exchange codes 114 to 117 for network testing in every area code (test numbers, not a drama range). There is no official example VAT number or company registration number, and no fictitious town or postcode; the UPU addressing examples use real towns. Luhn-valid VAT numbers starting with 4 (e.g. 4000000002) were not checked against the SARS register (interactive lookup only) and are left out. South Africa does not use IBAN, and no e-invoicing standard has been chosen yet.

identifiers.name: Income tax reference number
identifiers.notes: SARS "modulus 10" (PAYE Employer Reconciliation BRS, Appendix B) is Luhn on 10 digits. 9 = trusts and similar (Nature of Person E/G/H).

identifiers.name: PAYE / SDL / UIF reference number
identifiers.format: 7, L or U + 9 digits (same last 9 digits for all three)
identifiers.notes: Check digit = modulus 10 (Luhn) after replacing the first character with 4.

identifiers.name: VAT registration number
identifiers.notes: Check digit is probably the same modulus 10 rule; not confirmed for VAT in a SARS document.

identifiers.name: Enterprise (company registration) number
identifiers.notes: No check digit. Type codes (secondary sources, not verified) 06 public, 07 private (Pty) Ltd, 08 non-profit, 21 Inc, 23 close corporation.

identifiers.name: ID number
identifiers.format: 13 digits, YYMMDD SSSS C A Z
identifiers.notes: SSSS 5000-9999 = male; C 0 = citizen; Z = Luhn check digit.
